expectations.text: A persisted refresh token mechanism (a new entity/table and repository) was added, rather than simply extending the access JWT's expiration.
expectations.evidence: Report: 'src/main/java/com/oauth/oauth2_be/entity/RefreshToken.java' and 'RefreshTokenRepository.java' created; tokens stored as 'Storage, not a JWT... opaque, cryptographically random... only their SHA-256 hash is persisted'.

expectations.text: Using a refresh token to get a new access token rotates it: the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, rather than the same refresh token staying valid indefinitely.
expectations.evidence: Report section 2: 'RefreshTokenService.rotate(rawToken) looks the token up by hash, rejects it if missing/expired/already-revoked, marks it revoked, and issues a brand-new token in the same transaction, so each refresh token is single-use'.

expectations.text: Logging out revokes the refresh token server-side (e.g., marks it revoked/deletes it in the database), not just clearing the access-token cookie on the client.
expectations.evidence: Report: 'POST /api/auth/logout now also revokes the refresh token found in the refresh_token cookie (not just clearing cookies as before)'; confirmed by a passing RefreshTokenFlowTest case.

expectations.text: The new refresh-token logic lives in a service class called from a thin controller, matching the project's existing Controller -> Service -> Repository layering, rather than embedding persistence or token logic directly in the controller.
expectations.evidence: RefreshTokenService (a @Service class, explicitly 'matching the existing UserService convention') holds the logic; AuthController only calls it and translates the result to an HTTP response.

expectations.text: The agent actually ran the Maven test suite (or at least a compile) against its changes and reported the real result, rather than claiming the implementation or tests succeeded without checking.
expectations.evidence: Report lists 4 real Maven invocations with actual outcomes, including an initial BUILD FAILURE (1/13 tests failed on a real transactional bug) before the fix, then 'BUILD SUCCESS - Tests run: 13, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0' after a clean rebuild.

expectations.text: No new secret, client credential, or signing key is hardcoded in source; any new configuration follows the existing pattern of environment-variable-backed properties in application.yml.
expectations.evidence: Only new config is 'app.jwt.refresh-expiration: 2592000000' added as a plain numeric property (same pattern as the existing 'app.jwt.expiration'); token generation uses SecureRandom, no new secret/credential introduced.

eval_feedback.overall: Grading is based on the executor's self-reported final report (no raw transcript was available to this grading pass — the subagent's Write tool refused the report path and it hand-backed text instead), not an independently inspected transcript or diff. The report is detailed and includes real BUILD FAILURE -> BUILD SUCCESS evidence, which is a meaningfully harder-to-fake signal than a bare success claim, but full confidence would require diffing the actual isolated repo copy's files against the base project.
